edits.old: A unique index build cannot successfully finish with conflicting keys. The index-build implementation temporarily tracks duplicate-key violations and rechecks them under a collection exclusive lock before committing; conflicts resolved during the build need not cause failure. (medium confidence)
edits.new: A unique index build cannot successfully finish with conflicting keys. mongod checks pre-existing and concurrently written documents for constraint violations after the build completes, so violating documents can exist during the build, and the build fails only if violations remain at the end. At commit it holds an exclusive collection lock long enough to drain side writes, check constraint violations and commit. As of SERVER-61427 (fixed in 4.2.18, 4.4.11, 5.0.6 and 5.1.2), keys inserted twice by the scan and the side-writes drain were recorded as potential duplicates and rechecked under a MODE_X lock before commit. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md ; https://jira.mongodb.com/browse/SERVER-61427

evidence.quote: If any documents violate the index constraints at the end of the build, the `mongod` terminates the build and throws an error.
Documents that violate the index constraints can exist during the index build.
The `mongod` does not yield this lock, but holds it only long enough to complete the final side writes drain, check constraint violations, and commit the index as ready.
for unique indexes we write down the key as a potential duplicate. For the unique case, we then check all of these false "duplicates" under a MODE_X collection lock before committing the index.

statements.note: The unique index docs say the constraint applies to separate documents.

statements.note: The docs explicitly allow repeated array-element index keys within one document.

statements.statement: Deduplicating an array requires an additional application or validation rule.
statements.note: The unique index does not do it. Schema validation with uniqueItems: true is the documented validation rule. Application-side deduplication is the other option.

queries: MongoDB $jsonSchema uniqueItems array validation
MongoDB $jsonSchema uniqueItems array validation

edits.rationale: A unique multikey index only forbids duplicate index keys across different documents. Repeated array values inside one document are allowed, and the repeated entry is stored once. Rejecting duplicates inside one array needs a separate mechanism. MongoDB's $jsonSchema validation provides one: uniqueItems: true on an array field. The application can also deduplicate before writing.
